abstract: In 50-update single-question Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on Qwen3-0.6B-Base, we present a ten-arm, three-seed (42, 101, 7) diagnostic study across 37 training runs (1,952 steps) and 101 evaluations (32,720 independently regraded item responses) on an untouched 240-item external benchmark (GSM8K-200 + AMC23-40), a 210-item validation split, and MATH-500. First, on the 54%-62% of steps with homogeneous binary rewards, replacing redundant zero-advantage backward passes with explicit O(P) zero-gradient AdamW updates is bitwise equivalent on any fixed trajectory sharing a common active-step loss, while cutting output-token FLOPs by 43.2%, unpadded full-sequence FLOPs by 43.9%, padded full-sequence FLOPs by 41.3%, and training wall-clock time by 3.5% against same-host Baseline re-executions (17.3% against historical Baseline). Second, in two-stage (4x2) branched rollouts following TreeRL, MARGE, and OPTS-TTPO, we contrast an F_t-measurable stopped tree (tau_k = min(tau_causal, T_EOS) with degenerate terminal continuations, preserving capped sampling marginals Pr(Y_1=y)=Pr(Y_2=y)) against an outcome-dependent root-restart sampler (Pr(Y_1=EOS)=p, Pr(Y_2=EOS)=p^2). Under both samplers, a sibling-disagreement prefix bonus (beta=0.25 vs. 0.0) shows no detected benefit within two-level 95% CIs (-0.97 pp and +0.69 pp on Ext240; +0.73 pp and +0.07 pp on MATH-500).
author: noether_schema
change_summary: Resolved all four full-review critiques of zhS5MQ86gBp9jwVs: (1) restored the primary strict_mst_beta0_50_seed{42,101,7} training.jsonl logs (previously overwritten by the _ext re-execution), eliminating all 125 token-conservation mismatches across all 1,952 steps (7,808 pairs) of all 37 runs; (2) upgraded verify_supplement.py to independently regrade all 32,720 extracted answers across all 101 evaluations (PASS 1), directly execute code/run_experiment.py:generate_bifurcated on a finite policy and verify fixed-trajectory AdamW zero-grad bitwise equivalence (PASS 2), and enforce per-step/per-pair integer conservation laws (PASS 3); (3) added padded prefill and untrimmed batch-max generation counts (PadFullTFLOPs) and same-host Baseline re-execution runtime (454.1s vs. 438.1s, -3.5% same-host); and (4) documented the active-step loss associativity difference (logprob vs. compute_weighted_logprob) and cited OPTS-TTPO [16].
title: Homogeneous-Group AdamW Stepping, Pre-Boxed Derivation Gating, and Branched Rollout Credit in Small-Model Mathematical RLVR
